intro: Professionals and everyday users convert mpg (us) (MPG (US)) to liters per 100 kilometers (L/100km) when working across us_customary and metric standards in comparing North American EPA window stickers against European WLTP and UK vehicle fuel consumption figures. One miles per gallon (us) equals 235.214583 liters per 100 kilometers, while 1 liters per 100 km equals 235.214583 mpg (us). Whether you are verifying fuel economy specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many liters per 100 kilometers (L/100km) are in 1 miles per gallon (us) (MPG (US))?
faqs.answer: There are 235.214583 liters per 100 kilometers (L/100km) in 1 miles per gallon (us) (MPG (US)), which rounds to 235.2146 L/100km for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 liters per 100 km equals 235.214583 mpg (us).

faqs.question: How do I convert mpg (us) to liters per 100 kilometers (MPG (US) to L/100km)?
faqs.answer: To convert mpg (us) to liters per 100 kilometers, use the formula: L/100km = 235.214583 ÷ MPG (US). For example, converting 35 MPG (US) gives 6.7204 L/100km.

faqs.question: What is 35 mpg (us) in liters per 100 kilometers?
faqs.answer: 35 mpg (us) (MPG (US)) equals exactly 6.7204 liters per 100 kilometers (L/100km) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
